newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swiss business climate best, survey says.
newsitem.headline: Swiss business climate best, survey says.

text.p: Several smaller countries on the periphery of Europe won higher ratings for their business climate than economic superpowers France, Germany and Britain in a survey of business leaders released on Thursday.
Switzerland, Ireland, the Netherlands, Sweden and Israel received the highest ratings in the poll of senior executives published by the European Council of American Chambers of Commerce (ECACC).

The survey measured the views of ECACC members on political policy, economic environment, infrastructure, workers' issues and quality of life affecting a company's ability to do business in its host country.
"Certainly, not seeing Germany within the top five was somewhat surprising," director Noah Pines of Research & Forecasts, which conducted the survey, told a news conference.
With positions nine, 11 and 15 respectively, Germany, Britain and France were also behind Luxembourg, Norway and Austria in the survey.
Former communist countries Bulgaria, Poland, the Slovak republic and Romania scored the worst.
However, executives based in Bulgaria and Romania were among those who expressed the most hope about improving business conditions over the next five years.
In contrast, business chiefs in developed countries such as Britain, Belgium, Switzerland, Italy and Germany believed the business climate would get worse, the survey said.
The report, carried out in September and early October, was based on interviews with 737 executives at U.S. and European companies in 23 countries.
The survey's base of respondents varied greatly, from at most 90 executives interviewed in Switzerland to only 19 in Israel, both countries which won high grades.
The executives were asked only about the country in which they were based and ECACC stressed the subjective nature of the survey, saying it was based on the respondents' personal experiences.

"This information from the public opinion study provides useful guidance for U.S. businesses operating in Europe and for those considering entering or expanding facilities in Europe," said ECACC chairman Lee Huebner.
The chambers belonging to ECACC have a combined membership of 16,000 American and European companies.
The survey gave Ireland the best rating for favourable political environment, including government policy towards business, while Bulgaria came last.
Luxembourg was judged top when it came to economic environment, including currency stability and efficiency of the banking system, while Poland had the worst rating.

Ireland also won the highest grade for work-related factors, while Israel scored best on infrastructure issues and quality of life, including availability of good medical care and control of crime and corruption.
